title: Automated Laboratory Sample Processing
business: Clinical diagnostic laboratories managing high-throughput sample analysis.
problem: Manual tracking of sample states leads to race conditions, where samples are simultaneously marked as 'processing' and 'archived', causing data corruption and audit failures.
solution: XState enforces strict state transitions and event-driven logic, ensuring that a sample can only exist in one defined state at a time, preventing invalid concurrent operations.
steps: Define the machine states: Idle, Processing, Validating, and Archived.
Map explicit events like 'start_analysis', 'complete_analysis', and 'archive_sample' to trigger transitions.
Use the actor model to encapsulate the sample logic, ensuring each sample instance maintains its own isolated context.
Implement guard conditions to prevent transitions if the current context data is incomplete.
Subscribe to state changes to trigger external logging or database updates automatically.
outcome: A predictable, audit-ready workflow where every state change is traceable and illegal transitions are programmatically blocked.
limitation: State machines can become overly complex when handling deeply nested logic; developers must monitor the state graph size to ensure it remains maintainable and readable.
